label: Marketing breakdown
text:
When heritage brands pick a face, they usually look for fame.

Great brands look for absolute mastery.

Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea reportedly named A.R. Rahman as brand ambassador and launched the Awaken Your Masterpiece campaign.

It is a masterclass in aligning identity with craft.

Taj Mahal Tea has always leaned into artistry and classical notes.

By bringing in a musical legend, the brand does not just get a celebrity endorsement.

It reinforces its core positioning without saying a single extra word.

Here is what marketers can learn from this move:

1. Match the ethos → Pick partners who naturally embody your brand values.

2. Lead with craft → Campaigns built on true skill cut through the noise faster.

3. Honor heritage → Keep your long-term identity intact while staying fresh.

How do you usually evaluate a strong brand collaboration?

label: Personal Branding
text:
Your personal brand is not what you post.
It is what people say about you when you leave the room.
Most people spend hours designing a logo or writing a bio.
Then they forget the real work.
A strong brand is built in the quiet moments.
How you handle a missed deadline.
How you treat people who cannot help your career.
How consistently you show up with good work.
If you want to shape how people talk about you, try this.

-> Share your actual process, not just the polished final win.
-> Solve one specific problem for your audience every single week.
-> Be the person who makes complex ideas simple to understand.

People forget your posts in five minutes.
They remember how you made them feel.
What is one thing you want people to associate your name with?

label: Linkedin Growth
text:
Your first line on LinkedIn is your only chance to stop the scroll.
If it is boring, nobody reads the rest.

Most people start with a summary.
Or a corporate cliché.
That is why their posts get ignored.

A great hook does not give away the ending.
It creates a gap in the reader's brain.
It makes them need to know what happens next.

Here is how to write better hooks:
-> State a bold opinion that challenges the usual advice
-> Start with a short sentence that creates instant curiosity
-> Focus on a common mistake everyone makes but hates to admit

What is the best hook you have read recently?

label: Genz Careers
text:
Your first internship is not a test you need to ace silently.

Most young professionals think asking questions shows you are not prepared.

It actually shows you care about doing the work right.

Pretending to understand a brief to look smart always backfires.

Here is what you should do instead:

-> Clarify the goal before opening a blank document
-> Ask for examples of past good work to set your baseline
-> Schedule a quick sync when you feel stuck for more than twenty minutes
-> Remember that managers expect to guide beginners

Curiosity is a better career skill than pretending you know everything.

What is the best piece of advice you received during your first role?

label: Hot Takes
text:
Hustle culture on LinkedIn is a trap for young professionals.

Working twenty four seven is not a badge of honor.
It is a fast track to burnout.

We keep telling students and creators to sleep less and do more.
This advice ignores how real growth actually happens.

Real skill takes time to build.
Burnout stops you from thinking clearly.

Here is what to do instead

→ Focus on deep work over long hours
→ Protect your rest like it is a meeting
→ Measure output by value not time

How do you balance growth and rest?

#PersonalBranding #CareerAdvice #GenZ
